okay, so as noted Pinikir was definitively the Elamite interpretation of the Akkadian Inana and was seen at the time by both peoples as an equivalent deity
but there were some differences, mostly in terms of appearance

in particular Pinikir was generally described as bearing either two swords of different sizes or a sword and a shortspear, which would also mirror the weaponry sometimes used either ceremonially or actually by warriors who were devoted to Inana or otherwise guarded temples
and their weaponry and armor was made out of the bones of creatures adorned with additional gemstones

in terms of their role as deities

both were "chief deities" essentially, as in almost always given the highest ranking among local and tutelary deities, the demesnes that they both shared were of love, sex, war, transmutation and transformation, the enforcement of justice... there's many other things as well

in terms of differences Inana and Pinikir had, Inana is associated specifically with the Morning Star (and stars generally) whereas Pinikir is more associated with night and the lands, Pinikir also had more emphasis on their form being astral and not physically existing
also finally Inana was responsible for fecundity and fertility whereas that was passed to another deity in the Elamite pantheon
its already finished go read it
anyways, the main and most relevant thing is that the key role they have above all else in the importance of human societies is being the "maker" or the "chooser" of kings and high priestesses
they are seen as personally placing the crown upon them and granting them authority to rule, when that divine blessing is not present or is revoked, disaster generally would be believed to follow
although later in history certain rulers like the infamous Hammurabi after being scorned by Inana falsely claimed that Enlil had given them authority instead so their imposed rule was not voided
i think it's pretty likely the story is referential
what were the circumstances that would make a ruler lose their blessing?

well, as the "high lady" made them king and permitted them to be such, her favour would need to be maintained. Inana is not really a petty-minded deity in the sense of say, most of the "Greek" pantheon though... extensive corruption with their rule, committing injustice and telling lies before deities and courts, heavily disdaining Inana in favor of the Annunaki associated with the skies and committing war crimes were generally written as things that caused her to curse rulers or entire city-states

the reason I asked is because of this section from the šir-namursaĝa to Ninsiana [a dialect name for Inana] for Iddin-Dagan [on behalf of a king]

Their locks of hair at the back are adorned for her with coloured rags; they parade before her, holy Inana. Clothed in the leather of divinity, they parade before her, holy Inana. The trustworthy man and the proud lady, the doyenne of the great wise women, parade before her, holy Inana. Those who are in chargr of beating the soothing balaĝ drums parade before her, holy Inana. Each girded with a sword belt, the strength of battle, they parade before her, holy Inana. Grasping a spear, the strength of battle, in their hands, they parade before her, holy Inana. 

Young women, šugia priestesses, coiffured, parade before her, holy Inana. …… sword and dagger for her, they parade before her, holy Inana. With daggers in their hands, …… kurĝara priests parade before her, holy Inana. Those who cover their swords with gore spatter blood as they parade before her, holy Inana. Blood is poured on the dais standing in the guena hall, as tigi, šem and ala drums are made to sound loudly.

They pursue …… Inana ……, who are favoured by Inana's heart, who stand in the battle, they are the fourteen torches of battle ……, at midnight they ……, at dead of night they pursue like wildfire, in a band they flash together like lightning, in the urgent storm of battle, which roars loudly like a great flood rising up; they who are favoured in Inana's heart, who stand in the battle, they are the seven torches of battle ……; they stand joyfully as she wears the crown under a clear sky, with their foreheads and eyes they are a clear evening. Their ears …… a boat, with their mouths they are wild boars resting in a reed thicket; they stand in the thick of battle, with their life-force they ……,
